Narrow leather belt with a stringwork apron at the front, and an iron chain across the back with a patterned leather strip hanging from it [RTS 10/12/2004].

Cap made from beads and cord. Woven cord structure with a spiral of beads stitched to it; two red and blue geometric motifs on a white background; human hair and clay inside top of cap; loop of plant fibre from rim.

Chip. Skirt worn by married women. Plaited leather band with lots of metal loops attached to the outside. Leather fringe attached to the centre of the band. Small length of fibre wound around the band.

Leather belt with an iron chain apron hanging down at the front. The belt is made from braided leather, and is decorated with white opaque glass beads and two spiral wire beads. There are two strings of green and blue beads, one with four and one with five, hanging from a chain on one side of the apron.

Leather belt decorated with iron beads along both the upper and lower edge. The belt's fastening consists of three loops threaded with iron beads on one side, and two strips of leather for tying on the other side. One of the loops also has one blue glass bead and three white disc beads.
Apron of hide/skin. Rectangular piece of hide with with thin straps at both top corners. Some hair remains on the apron. Worn by men.
Leather belt, narrow band of leather with two leather straps at one end and a zig zag cutaway section at the other end.
Leather belt with an iron chain apron hanging down at the front. The belt is made from braided leather, and has strands of leather loose at both ends.

arms.title: Iron spear-butt of pointed quadrangular form, sometimes used as a drill. Socketed at the opposing end. [ASh [OPS move] 26/6/2017]
Iron spear-head with narrow leaf shaped blade and socketed base [RTS 24/6/2005].
Small circular shield of thick hide. For the wooden toggle see 1884.30.60 .2. [CW [OPS move] 10/8/2016]

Iron split socketed spearhead [A] and ferrule [B]. Spear has a leaf-shaped blade, with a prominent midrib. Ferrule has a square cross-section, and a split socket. Part of the wooden handle remains in the socket of the ferrule.

A bow harp with a curved wooden neck with five tuning peg holes with one tuning peg present, from which five strings are tied and connected to the sound box. The sound box is made from a tortoise shell covered in hide across the top, with two small holes cut out; the bottom is also covered in a small patch of hide stitched with lengths of hide. Two strings have been partially replaced with nylon thread.

A shield made from hide. Roughly rectangular with upward curving sides, a convex cross-section and tapering, extended ends. There are metal tacks used to secure leather in place and some which perforate the body of the shield. Central wooden stave handle on reverse bound round with hide thongs which pierce the shield at intervals; the grip is reinforced by an oval piece of hide. The stick extends beyond the body of the shield at one end and is decorated with a dense section of feathers; many of which have been eaten by pests. At the other end is a length of leather.

photo.title: A portrait of a seated Lango man sitting on a stool holding a pipe with his hair matted into a long section down his back. The image seems to have been taken sometime in January 1879 when Buchta travelled through Acholi and Lango country en route to Bunyoro.

A portrait of a seated Lango chief wearing an animal skin cloak and headdress of slender gourds, feathers and other attachments, almost certainly with ritual importance. The image seems to have been taken sometime in January 1879 when Buchta travelled through Acholi and Lango country en route to Bunyoro.

A youth smoothing a spear shaft through a hole in a tree, one of a series of images relating to Lango spear-making. It is likely that this print is a still taken from the cine-film made by Powell-Cotton during a hunting expedition in the Imatong hills.

A youth looking up a spear shaft that has been straightened by being bent using a hole in a tree, whilst another youth straightens another shaft in the hole, one of a series of images relating to Lango spear-making. It is likely that this print is a still taken from the cine-film made by Powell-Cotton during a hunting expedition in the Imatong hills.

Youth straightening spear shafts using a hole in a tree, one of a series of images relating to Lango spear-making. It is likely that this print is a still taken from the cine-film made by Powell-Cotton during a hunting expedition in the Imatong hills.

Lango men cutting and straightening spear shafts using a hole in a tree, one of a series of images relating to Lango spear-making. It is likely that this print is a still taken from the cine-film made by Powell-Cotton during a hunting expedition in the Imatong hills.
Group of six Umiro men in a homestead.
Group of three Umiro men holding spears in a homestead.
Upper body full face portrait Umiro man.

Side-blown trumpet carved from antelope horn with embouchure on convex side and finger-hole at proximal end, bound in hide and reptile skin with a long hair tassel, used in dances [RTS 24/1/2005].
Echoich. Horn war whistle wrapped in leather with a leather cap and plaited leather straps.

Pair of small penannular aluminium earrings, worn by a man [RTS 12/5/2004].

Rectangular hide strip, edged with blue and white glass beads with iron beads at one end, worn hanging down from the back of an apron by married women [RTS 13/12/2004].

Alyam. Neck ornament made from three tails attached to plaited leather straps; one of the tails is decorated with knotted additional hairs. The three straps are connected to an iron loop which joins an echoich (war whistle) made of a small horn wrapped in leather thongs with a leather strap extending from the back.

Frontlet made of beads worn on the forehead. Made of four strands of glass beads; four groups of white beads, two of small red beads, two of spherical, dark blue beads and one of spherical light and dark blue beads, and one pink bead. Groups of beads are separated with strips of leather.
Bead ornament/headdress. Multiple strings of beads bundled together with one large red bead. The strings are made up of white, yellow, green, blue and red beads. Probably a man's forehead band.
Akum. Arm ornament made of a leather band, with a bundle of black and blond hair, possibly the tail of a cow, attached. Wrrap of plant fibre around the arm band.

other.title: Heavy mallet carved from a single piece of wood [RTS 5/7/2004].

Two cow tails mounted on lengths of plaited leather; one with a leather cone to cover the join, one with a band of copper alloy. Each has a small horn whistle attached via a length of leather and wrapped in leather bands. Tied together with sinew.
An ivory arm band. Rectangular shape with worked ends that curve upwards. Large rectangular hole carved in the middle.
